claims.text: The North Sea lies between Great Britain and Scandinavia.
The Baltic Sea lies east of Scandinavia, the Irish Sea west of Great Britain and the Barents Sea north of Norway and Russia.
During the last ice age much of the North Sea basin was dry land, known as Doggerland.
People lived and hunted on Doggerland before rising seas flooded it.

evidence.restatement: The North Sea lies between Great Britain and Scandinavia.
The Baltic lies east of the Scandinavian Peninsula, the Irish Sea west of Great Britain and the Barents Sea north of Norway and Russia.
In the last ice age and after it, much of the southern North Sea basin was dry land now called Doggerland.
Mesolithic tools and bones dredged from the North Sea show people lived and hunted on Doggerland before it flooded.
The North Sea lies between Great Britain and Norway and Denmark (Scandinavia).
The Baltic Sea lies east of the Scandinavian peninsula's southern part, the Irish Sea between Great Britain and Ireland, and the Barents Sea north of Norway and Russia.
At the last glacial maximum much of the North Sea basin, including the southern part called Doggerland, was dry land or ice-covered.
Mesolithic people lived and hunted on Doggerland before rising seas flooded it.
